analyzed_vuln.description: `get_coffset` calls `blosc2_getitem(coffsets, off_cbytes, nchunk, 1, offset, sizeof(int64_t))` on attacker-controlled compressed `coffsets` data from the frame without validating that the decoded offsets chunk header fields are sane. This allows malformed offsets-chunk metadata (notably blocksize/typesize-derived values) to propagate into `_blosc_getitem`/`blosc_d`, where `neblock` becomes negative and is cast to unsigned in `memset(_dest, 0, (unsigned int)neblock)`, triggering ASan negative-size-param. Crash manifests in `blosc_d` but root cause is missing validation of offsets chunk before using `blosc2_getitem` in `get_coffset`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer provides a crafted frame buffer to `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer`; during `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_get_lazychunk`, the code needs chunk offsets and invokes `get_coffset`. If the embedded compressed offsets chunk is malformed so that `blosc2_getitem` reaches `blosc_d` with inconsistent header values (e.g., causing negative `neblock`), the memset path for `cbytes==0`/run-length handling uses a huge unsigned size and crashes with negative-size-param.
